text:
- JDK 17
- Apache Maven 3.8+
- GnuPG 2.1+
- Git
- SVN

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Preparation > GPG signature
text:
Follow the Apache release guidelines, you need the GPG signature to sign the release version, users can also use this to determine if the downloaded version has been tampered with.

Create a pgp key for version signing, use `<your Apache ID>@apache.org` as the USER-ID for the key.

For more details, refer to [Apache Releases Signing documentation](https://infra.apache.org/release-signing)，[Cryptography with OpenPGP](http://www.apache.org/dev/openpgp.html).

Brief process for generating a key：

* Generate a new GPG key using `gpg --gen-key`, set the key length to 4096 and set it to never expire
* Upload the key to the public key server using `gpg --keyserver keys.openpgp.org --send-key <your key id>`
* Export the public key to a text file using `gpg --armor --export <your key id> >> gpgapachekey.txt`
* Obtain the keys of other committers for signing (optional)
* Add the generated key to the KEYS file (uploaded to the svn repository by the release manager)

You can follow the steps below to create the GPG key:

{{< hint info >}}
You should replace `amoro` with your `Apache ID` in following guides.
{{< /hint >}}

```shell
$ gpg --full-gen-key
gpg (GnuPG) 2.2.27; Copyright (C) 2021 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software: you are free to change and redistribute it.
There is NO WARRANTY, to the extent permitted by law.

Please select what kind of key you want:
(1) RSA and RSA (default)
(2) DSA and Elgamal
(3) DSA (sign only)
(4) RSA (sign only)
(14) Existing key from card
Your selection? 1 # Please enter 1
RSA keys may be between 1024 and 4096 bits long.
What keysize do you want? (3072) 4096 # Please enter 4096 here
Requested keysize is 4096 bits
Please specify how long the key should be valid.
0 = key does not expire
<n> = key expires in n days
<n>w = key expires in n weeks
<n>m = key expires in n months
<n>y = key expires in n years
Key is valid for? (0) 0 # Please enter 0
Key does not expire at all
Is this correct? (y/N) y # Please enter y here

GnuPG needs to construct a user ID to identify your key.

Real name: amoro # Please enter 'gpg real name'
Email address: amoro@apache.org # Please enter your apache email address here
Comment: amoro # Please enter some comments here
You selected this USER-ID:
    "amoro (amoro) <amoro@apache.org>"

Change (N)ame, (C)omment, (E)mail or (O)kay/(Q)uit? O # Please enter O here
We need to generate a lot of random bytes. It is a good idea to perform
some other action (type on the keyboard, move the mouse, utilize the
disks) during the prime generation; this gives the random number
generator a better chance to gain enough entropy.

# At this time, a dialog box will pop up, asking you to enter the key for this gpg. 
# you need to remember that it will be used in subsequent steps.
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Please enter this passphrase to                     │
│ protect your new key                                │
│                                                     │
│ Passphrase: _______________________________________ │
│                                                     │
│     <OK>                    <Cancel>                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

# Here you need to re-enter the password in the previous step.
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Please re-enter this passphrase                     │
│                                                     │
│ Passphrase: _______________________________________ │
│                                                     │
│     <OK>                    <Cancel>                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
gpg: key ACFB69E705016886 marked as ultimately trusted
gpg: revocation certificate stored as '/root/.gnupg/openpgp-revocs.d/DC12398CCC33A5349EB9663DF9D970AB18C9EDF6.rev'
public and secret key created and signed.

pub   rsa4096 2023-05-01 [SC]
      85778A4CE4DD04B7E07813ABACFB69E705016886
uid                      amoro (amoro) <amoro@apache.org>
sub   rsa4096 2023-05-01 [E]

```

Then you can follow the steps below to upload the GPG key to the public server:

```shell
$ gpg --keyid-format SHORT --list-keys
/root/.gnupg/pubring.kbx
------------------------
pub   rsa4096/05016886 2023-05-01 [SC]
      85778A4CE4DD04B7E07813ABACFB69E705016886
uid         [ultimate] amoro (amoro) <amoro@apache.org>
sub   rsa4096/0C5A4E1C 2023-05-01 [E]

# Send public key to keyserver via key id
$ gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --send-key 05016886 # send key should be found in the --list-keys result
# Among them, keyserver.ubuntu.com is the selected keyserver, it is recommended to use this, because the Apache Nexus verification uses this keyserver
```

Check if the key is uploaded successfully:

```shell
$ gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys 05016886   # If the following content appears, it means success
gpg: key ACFB69E705016886: "amoro (amoro) <amoro@apache.org>" not changed
gpg: Total number processed: 1
gpg:              unchanged: 1

```

Add the GPG public key to the KEYS file of the Apache SVN project warehouse:

```shell
# Add public key to KEYS in dev branch
$ mkdir -p ~/amoro_svn/dev
$ cd ~/amoro_svn/dev
$ svn co https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/incubator/amoro
$ cd ~/amoro_svn/dev/amoro
# Append the KEY you generated to the file KEYS, and check if it is added correctly
$ (gpg --list-sigs amoro@apache.org && gpg --export --armor amoro@apache.org) >> KEYS 

$ svn ci -m "add gpg key for amoro"

# Add public key to KEYS in release branch
$ mkdir -p ~/amoro_svn/release
$ cd ~/amoro_svn/release

$ svn co https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/release/incubator/amoro/
$ cd ~/amoro_svn/release/amoro

# Append the KEY you generated to the file KEYS, and check if it is added correctly
$ (gpg --list-sigs amoro@apache.org && gpg --export --armor amoro@apache.org) >> KEYS 

$ svn ci -m "add gpg key for amoro"
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Preparation > Maven settings
text:
During the release process, frequent access to your Apache password is required. To prevent exposure in plaintext storage, we need to encrypt it.

```shell
# Generate master password
$ mvn --encrypt-master-password <apache password>
{EM+4/TYVDXYHRbkwjjAS3mE1RhRJXJUSG8aIO5RSxuHU26rKCjuS2vG+/wMjz9te}
```

Create the file `${user.home}/.m2/settings-security.xml` and configure the password created in the previous step:

```xml
<settingsSecurity>
 <master>{EM+4/TYVDXYHRbkwjjAS3mE1RhRJXJUSG8aIO5RSxuHU26rKCjuS2vG+/wMjz9te}</master>
</settingsSecurity>
```

In the maven configuration file `~/.m2/settings.xml`, add the following item:

```xml
<settings xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/SETTINGS/1.0.0"
  xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/SETTINGS/1.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/settings-1.0.0.xsd">
  
  <servers>
    <server>
        <id>apache.snapshots.https</id>
         
        <username>amoro</username>
        
        <password>{/ZLaH78TWboH5IRqNv9pgU4uamuqm9fCIbw0gRWT01c=}</password>
    </server>
    <server>
        <id>apache.releases.https</id>
         
        <username>amoro</username>
        
        <password>{/ZLaH78TWboH5IRqNv9pgU4uamuqm9fCIbw0gRWT01c=}</password>
    </server>
  </servers>

  <profiles>
        <profile>
          <id>apache-release</id>
          <properties>
            <gpg.keyname>05016886</gpg.keyname>
            
            <gpg.useagent>true</gpg.useagent>
            <gpg.passphrase>passphrase for your gpg key</gpg.passphrase>
          </properties>
        </profile>
  </profiles>
</settings>
```

Generate the final encrypted password and add it to the `~/.m2/settings.xml` file:

```shell
$ mvn --encrypt-password <apache password>
{/ZLaH78TWboH5IRqNv9pgU4uamuqm9fCIbw0gRWT01c=}
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Build release > Cut the release branch
text:
> The version of Apache Amoro follows the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/), which looks like `{major}.{mior}.{patch}`

Cut a branch for the `minor` version if it is not created in the Apache remote repository, if it already exists, check it out and pull the latest changes.

```shell
$ cd ${AMORO_SOURCE_HOME}

# Cut the release branch if it is not created, then push to the remote 
$ git checkout -b 0.8.x
$ git push apache 0.8.x

# Or check it out and pull the latest changes if it is created
$ git checkout 0.8.x
$ git pull apache 0.8.x
```

Checkout a `patch` branch using the following command
```
$ git checkout -b 0.8.0-branch
```

Update the version in the new branch using the tool `tools/change-version.sh`:
```bash
OLD="0.8-SNAPSHOT"
NEW="0.8.0-incubating"

HERE=` basename "$PWD"`
if [[ "$HERE" != "tools" ]]; then
    echo "Please only execute in the tools/ directory";
    exit 1;
fi

# change version in all pom files
find .. -name 'pom.xml' -type f -exec perl -pi -e 's#<version>'"$OLD"'</version>#<version>'"$NEW"'</version>#' {} \;
```

Then run the scripts and commit the change:

```shell
$ cd tools
$ bash change-version.sh
$ cd ..
$ git add *
$ git commit -m "Change project version to 0.8.0-incubating"
$ git push apache 0.8.0-branch
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Build release > Create the release tag
text:
Create the release tag and push it to the Apache repo:

```shell
$ git tag -a v0.8.0-rc1 -m "Release Apache Amoro 0.8.0 rc1"
$ git push apache v0.8.0-rc1
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Build release > Build binary and source release
text:
Build Amoro binary release with scripts:

```shell
$ cd ${AMORO_SOURCE_HOME}/tools
$ RELEASE_VERSION=0.8.0-incubating bash ./releasing/create_binary_release.sh
```

Then build source release with scripts:

```shell
$ cd ${AMORO_SOURCE_HOME}/tools
$ RELEASE_VERSION=0.8.0-incubating bash ./releasing/create_source_release.sh
```

Validate the source and binary packages according to the [How to validate a new release](../validate-release/) guides.
After that, publish the dev directory of the Apache SVN warehouse of the material package:

```shell
$ cd ~/amoro_svn/dev/amoro
$ mkdir 0.8.0-incubating-RC1
$ cp ${AMORO_SOURCE_HOME}/tools/releasing/release/* 0.8.0-incubating-RC1
$ svn add 0.8.0-incubating-RC1
$ svn commit -m "Release Apache Amoro 0.8.0 rc1"

```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Build release > Release Apache Nexus
text:
Next, we will publish the required JAR files to the ​Apache Nexus​ repository to achieve the final goal of releasing them to the ​Maven Central Repository.

```shell
$ cd ${$AMORO_SOURCE_HOME}/tools
$ RELEASE_VERSION=0.8.0-incubating bash ./releasing/deploy_staging_jars.sh
```

You can visit https://repository.apache.org/ and log in to check the publishment status. You can find the publishment process in the `Staging Repositories` section. You need to close the process when all jars are publised.

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Vote for the new release
text: Next, vote for the new release via email. First complete the vote within the Amoro community, and upon approval, complete the vote within the Amoro community in the Incubator community. For detailed voting guidelines, please refer to [voting process](https://www.apache.org/foundation/voting.html).

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Vote for the new release > Vote in the Amoro community
text:
Send a vote email to `dev@amoro.apache.org` to start the vote process in Apache Amoro community, you can take [[VOTE] Release Apache Amoro(incubating) 0.8.0-incubating rc3](https://lists.apache.org/thread/22rrpzwtzkby8vnhfvcwzmpfxxz8qhns) as an example.

You can validate the source and binary packages according to the [How to validate a new release](../validate-release/) guides and give your vote resulut. If other developers identify critical issues, you need to cancel the current vote, wait for the fixes to be implemented, and then restart the release process with a new release candidate.

After 72 hours, if there are at least 3 binding votes from Amoro PPMC members and no votes against, send the result email to celebrate the release of the version like [[RESULT][VOTE] Release Apache Amoro(incubating) 0.8.0-incubating rc3](https://lists.apache.org/thread/gokj30ldgh3p5866tw40h41mhdw90whs).

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Vote for the new release > Vote in the Incubator community
text:
> We recommend to use gmail when sending the email.

Send a vote email to `general@incubator.apache.org` to start the vote process in Apache Incubator community, you can take [[VOTE] Release Apache Amoro(incubating) 0.8.0-incubating rc3](https://lists.apache.org/thread/bqj7gohrjwxp5gwycdgh78xmpymfm6jr) as an example.

After 72 hours, if there are at least 3 binding votes from IPMC members and no votes against, send the result email to celebrate the release of the version like [[RESULT][VOTE] Release Apache Amoro(incubating) 0.8.0-incubating rc3](https://lists.apache.org/thread/qmvg3tcds0p0pbn05w0mzchm85o581rv).

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Complete the final publishing steps > Migrate source and binary packages
text:
Migrate the source and binary packages to the release directory of the Apache SVN warehouse:

```shell
$ svn mv https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/incubator/amoro/0.8.0-incubating-RC1 https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/release/incubator/amoro/0.8.0-incubating  -m "Release Apache Amoro 0.8.0-incubating"
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Complete the final publishing steps > Publish releases in the Apache Staging repository
text:
- Log in to http://repository.apache.org , log in with your Apache account
- Click Staging repositories on the left
- Select your most recently uploaded warehouse, the warehouse specified in the voting email
- Click the Release button above, this process will perform a series of checks

> It usually takes 24 hours for the warehouse to synchronize to other data sources

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Complete the final publishing steps > Add release note and update the main web
text:
- Creating an [new release note](https://github.com/apache/amoro/releases) in github
- Update the content for the new version for the web, the source locates in [amoro-site](https://github.com/apache/amoro-site) repo
  - First, submit a pull request containing the new version. You can refer to [this commit](https://github.com/apache/amoro-site/commit/598787c97898bb6431686e9cf6dd37f89ce2a339). Note that the `$version` in the "url = "/docs/$version/" URL in hugo.toml corresponds to the branch name will be created in the following step in amoro-site
  - After merging the pull request from step 1, pull a local branch named `$version` and push it remotely
  - Check that the [GithubAction](https://github.com/apache/amoro-site/actions/workflows/deploy.yml) for branch `$version` is executed successfully

page_title: olake-fusion: How to release a new version
heading: Complete the final publishing steps > Send announcement email
text:
Finally, we need to send the announcement email to these mailing lists: `dev@amoro.apache.org`, `general@incubator.apache.org`. Here is an example of an announcement email:  [[ANNOUNCE] Apache Amoro (Incubating) 0.8.0-incubating available](https://lists.apache.org/thread/h3cy8f2mfmp4zms4cs3tq4hdlq64qyw0).

Congratulations! You have successfully completed all steps of the Apache Amoro release process. Thank you for your contributions!

# How to validate a new release

page_title: olake-fusion: How to validate a new release
heading: Download candidate
text:
```shell
# If there is svn locally, you can clone to the local
$ svn co https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/incubator/amoro/${release_version}-${rc_version}/
# or download the material file directly
$ wget https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/incubator/amoro/${release_version}-${rc_version}/
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to validate a new release
heading: validate candidate > Check GPG signature
text:
Download the KEYS and import it:

```shell
$ curl  https://downloads.apache.org/incubator/amoro/KEYS > KEYS # Download KEYS
$ gpg --import KEYS # Import KEYS to local
```

Trust the KEY used in this version:

```shell
$ gpg --edit-key xxxxxxxxxx #KEY user used in this version
gpg (GnuPG) 2.2.21; Copyright (C) 2020 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software: you are free to change and redistribute it.
There is NO WARRANTY, to the extent permitted by law.

Secret key is available.
gpg> trust #trust
Please decide how far you trust this user to correctly verify other users' keys
(by looking at passports, checking fingerprints from different sources, etc.)

  1 = I don't know or won't say
  2 = I do NOT trust
  3 = I trust marginally
  4 = I trust fully
  5 = I trust ultimately
  m = back to the main menu

Your decision? 5 #choose 5
Do you really want to set this key to ultimate trust? (y/N) y  #choose y
```

Check the gpg signature:

```shell
$ for i in *.tar.gz; do echo $i; gpg --verify $i.asc $i; done
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to validate a new release
heading: validate candidate > Check sha512 hash
text:
```shell
# Command for Linux
$ for i in *.tar.gz; do echo $i; sha512sum --check  $i.sha512; done
# Command for MacOS
$ for i in *.tar.gz; do echo $i; shasum -a 512 -c $i.sha512; done
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to validate a new release
heading: validate candidate > Check the binary package
text:
Unzip the binary pakcages: `apache-amoro-${AMORO_VERSION}-bin-${HADOOP_VERSION}.tar.gz`:

```shell
# Hadoop2
$ tar -xzvf apache-amoro-0.8.0-incubating-bin-hadoop2.tar.gz

# Hadoop3 
$ tar -xzvf apache-amoro-0.8.0-incubating-bin-hadoop3.tar.gz
```

check as follows:
- Check whether the package contains unnecessary files, which makes the tar package too large
- Folder contains the word incubating
- There are LICENSE and NOTICE files
- There is a DISCLAIMER file
- Check for extra files or folders, such as empty folders, etc.

page_title: olake-fusion: How to validate a new release
heading: validate candidate > Check the source package
text:
Unzip the binary pakcages: `apache-amoro-${AMORO_VERSION}-src.tar.gz`:

```shell
$ tar -xzvf apache-amoro-0.8.0-incubating-src.tar.gz
```

Check as follows:
- There are LICENSE and NOTICE files
- There is a DISCLAIMER file
- All source files have ASF license at the beginning
- Only source files exist, not binary files

Compile from source:

```shell
# Compile from source
$ mvn clean package

# Or skip the unit test
$ mvn clean package -DskipTests
```

page_title: olake-fusion: How to validate a new release
heading: vote for the release
text:
If all verifications pass, please vote +1 for the new release! If you find any critical issues, pleaste vote -1 for it.
Thanks a lot for your work!

# Quickstart

This guide outlines the basic process of using Amoro, allowing you to quickly experience its core features. You can choose to use either the `Iceberg Format` or the `Mixed-Iceberg Format` to complete the entire process. 

If you are more interested in the `Mixed-Hive Format` or the `Paimon Format`, you can refer to: [Mixed-Hive Format](/docs/latest/mixed-hive-format/) and [Paimon Format](/docs/latest/paimon-format/). For specific information on the different formats supported by Amoro, please refer to: [Table Format](/docs/latest/formats-overview/).

Before starting the quick demo, some steps are required to prepare the environment. The fastest way to get started is to use a docker-compose file that uses the apache/amoro image. To use this, you'll need to install the [Docker CLI](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) as well as the [Docker Compose CLI](https://github.com/docker/compose-cli/blob/main/INSTALL.md).

Once you have those, save the yaml below into a file named docker-compose.yml:
```yaml
version: "3"
services:
  minio:
    image: olakego/minio
    container_name: minio
    environment:
      - MINIO_ROOT_USER=admin
      - MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=password
      - MINIO_DOMAIN=minio
    networks:
      amoro_network:
        aliases:
          - warehouse.minio
    ports:
      - 9001:9001
      - 9000:9000
    command: [ "server", "/data", "--console-address", ":9001" ]
  mc:
    depends_on:
      - minio
    image: olakego/mc
    container_name: mc
    networks:
      amoro_network:
    environment:
      - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=admin
      - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=password
      - AWS_REGION=us-east-1
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
      until (/usr/bin/mc alias set minio http://minio:9000 admin password) do echo '...waiting...' && sleep 1; done;
      /usr/bin/mc rm -r --force minio/warehouse;
      /usr/bin/mc mb minio/warehouse;
      /usr/bin/mc anonymous set public minio/warehouse;
      tail -f /dev/null
      "
  amoro:
    image: apache/amoro
    container_name: amoro
    ports:
      - 8081:8081
      - 1630:1630
      - 1260:1260
    environment:
      - JVM_XMS=1024
    networks:
      amoro_network:
    volumes:
      - ./amoro:/tmp/warehouse
    command: ["/entrypoint.sh", "ams"]
    tty: true
    stdin_open: true

networks:
  amoro_network:
    driver: bridge
```
Next, start up the docker containers with this command:
```shell
docker-compose up
```

heading: Prepare steps > Create optimizer group
text:
Open [http://localhost:1630](http://localhost:1630) in a browser, enter `admin/admin` to log in to the dashboard.

Click on `Optimizing` in the sidebar, choose `Optimizer Groups` and click `Add Group` button to create a new group befre creating catalog:

![Create group](../images/quickstart/create-group.png)

heading: Prepare steps > Create catalog
Prepare steps > Start optimizers
text:
Click on `Optimizing` in the sidebar, select the `Optimizers` tab, and click the `Create Optimizer` button.

![Scale out optimizer](../images/quickstart/create-optimizer.png)

Choose the `local` resource group and set the concurrency of the optimizer to 1 and click `OK`.

You may need to wait a few seconds and try refreshing the page, you will find the newly launched optimizer here.

![Optimizers](../images/quickstart/optimizers.png)

{{< hint info >}}
You may need to wait for up to 30 seconds for the optimizer to register with AMS.
{{< /hint >}}

heading: Demo steps > Initialize tables
Demo steps > Make some changes
Demo steps > Check self-optimizing
text:
As new data is written to the table, Amoro will automatically trigger self-optimizing on the table.

Click on `Tables` in the sidebar, select the test table to enter the table details page, and switch to the `Optimizing` tab, where you can see all the self-optimizing tasks on the table.

![Table optimizing history](../images/quickstart/table-optimizing-history.png)

You can also enter the `Optimizing` page through the sidebar to view the current optimizing status of all tables.

![Table optimizing status](../images/quickstart/table-optimizing-status.png)

For more information on Self-Optimizing, please refer to: [Self-optimizing](/docs/latest/self-optimizing/)

{{< hint info >}}
After finishing the demo, you can run the following command in the directory of docker-compose.yml to stop all containers:
{{< /hint >}}
```shell
docker-compose down
```

The Amoro theme is a theme for use with [Hugo](https://gohugo.io/).

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1306: Postgres ctid chunk splitter ignores TOAST, producing enormous chunks (~11 h each) so an interrupted sync commits nothing
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

For a Postgres table whose size is dominated by TOASTed `jsonb`, the ctid splitter sizes chunks from
`relpages` (main heap only). TOAST is a separate relation and is invisible to that calculation, so a
4.5 TB table was split into **9 chunks** that OLake believed were 2 GB each but which actually carried
**~1.2 TB / ~9.8M rows** each — a ~640x underestimate.

Because the Iceberg commit happens once per chunk at writer close, the first possible commit was ~11
hours in. Two runs were interrupted before any chunk completed, so **12.5 hours of reading produced 0
committed rows** (0 snapshots on the destination table) and no resumable state.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OLake | v0.12.0 (`olakego/source-postgres:v0.12.0`) |
| Source | PostgreSQL 18.4, `update_method: Standalone`, `max_threads: 2`, `retry_count: 5` |
| Destination | Iceberg, REST catalog (Lakekeeper 0.10.4), S3-compatible (Wasabi), legacy writer (`arrow_writes` unset) |
| Deployment | OLake UI + workers on GKE (olake-helm) |
| Stream | Full Refresh + Incremental, cursor `id`, no `chunk_column` |

## Source table profile

```
rows          : 78,523,153
main heap     :    16 GB      <- what relpages measures
TOAST         : 4,488 GB      <- two jsonb columns
indexes       :    23 GB
total         : 4,527 GB
avg payload   : ~131 KB of JSON per row
rows per page : ~37  (78.5M rows / 2,097,152 heap pages)
```

## What happens

`drivers/postgres/internal/backfill.go` (`generateCTIDRanges`, non-partitioned…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @AvinashKumar0923 please try out the olake version `0.12.1` and verify if the fix is working for you

- none: > 2\. [@AvinashKumar0923](https://github.com/AvinashKumar0923) please try out the olake version `0.12.1` and verify if the fix is working for you

Thanks @mihir-datazip for the quick fix in #1309.

I haven’t re-run this table on 0.12.1 yet. My backfill already finished using the chunk_column: id workaround, and I didn’t want to re-read 4.5 TB just to verify. I went through the PR against this table’s profile, and the numbers match: PG 18 takes the TID-range path, and table-size-based page sizing gives about 931 pages per chunk, about 2,251 chunks of about 35K rows each. At our measured throughput that means a commit roughly every 1.5–3 min instead of every ~11 h. A preemption like run 2’s would then lose at most the in-flight chunks rather than the whole 12.5 h. Using live pg_relation_size instead of relpages also removes the stale-ANALYZE concern I raised.

One note for anyone upgrading mid-backfill: existing state.json chunks are reused, so the state needs clearing for the new sizing to apply.

Closing this one; I’ll reopen if the next full refresh on 0.12.1 shows anything off.

Issue (completed): **Title:** MySQL CDC permanently fails on MariaDB with `ERROR 1236: Failed to replace GTID event with backwards-compatible event: corrupt event`

---

## Environment

- **Deploy method**: Kubernetes (OLake Helm chart on Amazon EKS, using `olakego/k8s-worker`)
- **Olake version**: `olakego/source-mysql:v0.6.4` (worker `olakego/k8s-worker:latest`). The code path is unchanged on `master` / `v0.11.3`.
- **OS**: Amazon Linux 2023 nodes on EKS 1.34 (amd64 and arm64)
- **Cloud Provider**: AWS. Source database is Amazon RDS for MariaDB `10.11.13-MariaDB-log`.
- **Docker Params (if deployed with docker)**: Not deployed with Docker. Relevant settings:
  - Source: MySQL connector pointed at RDS MariaDB, port `3306`, sync mode CDC
  - MariaDB: `binlog_format=ROW`, RDS binlog retention `168` hours, `binlog_commit_wait_count=0`
  - Worker env: `RUN_MODE=staging`, `IMAGE_PULL_POLICY=Always`, `TEMPORAL_TASK_QUEUE=OLAKE_DOCKER_TASK_QUEUE`
  - Volumes: shared state PVC (NFS) mounted into the worker and sync pods

## Description

Follow-up to #688, as requested there by @saksham-datazip.

Three CDC jobs reading from RDS for MariaDB started failing on the same binlog event and cannot recover. Every retry resumes from the saved binlog position and fails on the same event. The event is RDS's own housekeeping transaction (`DELETE FROM mysql.rds_sysinfo ...`), so it can show up on any RDS MariaDB instance, whatever the workload.

The cause is that `prepareBinlogConn` hardcodes `Flavor: "mysql"` for …

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1242: kafka discover: ProduceSchema discards fetch and schema-resolution errors, silently producing an empty or partial schema
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`ProduceSchema` drops errors at two levels, so a topic whose messages could not be fetched or resolved is reported as a successfully-discovered stream with a missing or incomplete schema.

## The path

In `drivers/kafka/internal/kafka.go:249-265`:

```go
_ = k.processKafkaMessages(ctx, reader, func(record types.KafkaRecord) (bool, error) {
    messageCount++
    if record.Data != nil {
        mu.Lock()
        err := typeutils.Resolve(stream, record.Data)
        mu.Unlock()
        if err != nil {
            return true, err   // (a) propagated to processKafkaMessages...
        }
    }
    shouldExit := messageCount >= 10000 || record.Message.Offset >= endOffset.Offset-1
    return shouldExit, nil
})
return nil                      // (b) ...and then thrown away here
```

- **(a) → (b)**: `typeutils.Resolve` failures are returned from the callback, `processKafkaMessages` propagates them, and the `_ =` assignment discards the result.
- The per-partition closure then unconditionally `return nil`, so `utils.Concurrent` sees every partition as successful and the `if err != nil` check at line 267 can never fire for these causes.
- The same discard hides fetch-side failures: `processKafkaMessages` wraps genuine fetch errors as `constants.ErrNonRetryable` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:271-273`), and those are discarded too.

## Impact

Discover reports success for a topic it could not actually read. The resulting stream has no resolved columns beyond the `_kafka_*`…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama Discover samples the first 10,000 messages to infer the stream schema. Columns that appear later are handled by schema evolution during sync, so a partial sample does not block the pipeline. Non-JSON messages are skipped during sampling. Could you let us know if this has caused any problems on your side?

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1241: kafka: ReaderManager.exitMode is never reset and is shared by all readers, so one rebalance halts every reader for the rest of the sync
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`ReaderManager.exitMode` (`pkg/kafka/types.go:41`) is a single `atomic.Int32` on the manager, shared by every reader in the group. Two problems follow from that.

### 1. It is never reset

`exitMode` is only ever written to a *terminal* value — `gracefulExit` or `nonRetryableExit` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:316`, `pkg/kafka/reader.go:323`). Nothing ever stores `normalProcessing` back. `RestartReader` recreates the franz-go client but leaves `exitMode` untouched (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:273-292`).

So once any rebalance fires, every subsequent retry attempt short-circuits immediately: `processKafkaMessages` checks `FetchExitState()` before its first poll (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:250-252`) and returns straight away. The retry driven by `RetryOnBackoff` (`utils/utils.go:482`) burns its attempts without ever reading a record.

### 2. It is global, not per-reader

The driver runs readers in parallel — `ChangeStreamConfig` returns `parallel=true` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:24-26`), and `drivers/abstract/cdc.go:82` fans out one goroutine per reader index. All of them share one `ReaderManager` and therefore one `exitMode`.

A rebalance callback on **one** reader sets the flag for **all** of them. Readers that still hold valid, unaffected partition assignments stop mid-partition too. Combined with issue #1240 (graceful exit reported as success → offsets committed), a single rebalance on one reader can cause short reads to be committed across every partition in the sync…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama Sharing exitMode across readers, and not resetting it after a rebalance, is by design.

When a rebalance is detected, we gracefully stop the sync. At that point, all readers need to stop consuming further records; otherwise, there is a risk of duplicate processing because their partition assignments may no longer be valid.

During the retry, static membership prevents another rebalance from being triggered. As a result, the exit mode is not changed back at that point, and the readers continue with the existing exit state.

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1240: kafka: graceful rebalance exit is reported as success, committing offsets for partitions that were never fully read
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

When a consumer group rebalance is detected mid-sync, the Kafka driver stops processing and reports **success**, which causes `PostCDC` to commit offsets. Because the partitions were only partially consumed, the unread remainder is skipped permanently on the next run.

## The path

1. `kgo.OnPartitionsAssigned` / `OnPartitionsRevoked` fire → `r.exitMode.Store(gracefulExit)` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:312-318`).
2. `FetchExitState()` returns `(stop=true, err=nil)` for `gracefulExit` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:359-361`).
3. `processKafkaMessages` sees `stopProcessing==true, err==nil` and returns `nil` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:250-252`).
4. `StreamChanges` gets `err == nil`, so it skips the error return and proceeds to build `metadataByStream` from whatever landed in `lastMessages` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:146-171`).
5. `streamChanges` in `drivers/abstract/cdc.go:107-111` runs the deferred `PostCDC` — which calls `reader.CommitRecords(ctx, messages...)` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:218`).

The committed offset is the last record processed *before the rebalance interrupted us*, not the partition end offset. On the next sync `PartitionsForStream` skips everything at or below that committed offset (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:139-142`), so the records between the interrupt point and `EndOffset` are never read.

A rebalance is a normal, expected event (a member joining/leaving, a session timeout, a coordinator move). Treating it as a clean completion turns a routine even…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama The statement that the records between the interruption point and `EndOffset` are never read is not correct. The committed offset is intentionally the last successfully processed record before the rebalance, rather than the partition's `EndOffset`.

On the next sync, `PartitionsForStream` resumes from the committed offset, so records after the interruption point are still consumed. We also emit a `Warnf` log when the sync is stopped gracefully.

This behavior is intentional and ensures that rebalances are handled safely without data loss.

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1239: kafka source: Avro/Protobuf wire-format messages silently mis-decoded as JSON when schema_registry is not configured
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go` `parseKafkaData`/`parseData` detects Confluent wire-format messages (`isConfluentWireFormat`, magic byte `0x00` + 4-byte schema ID) but when `schema_registry` is not configured, it unconditionally treats the payload as JSON:

```go
if isConfluentWireFormat(data) {
    if k.schemaRegistryClient == nil {
        return decodeJSONMessage(data[5:])
    }
    ...
```

If the topic actually contains Avro- or Protobuf-encoded data (which is the common case when wire-format framing is present at all — plain JSON producers rarely emit the magic byte), this attempts to JSON-decode raw binary Avro/Protobuf bytes. Best case this fails with a confusing `invalid character ...` JSON parse error that gives no hint that a schema registry is required; worst case (rare, if the binary happens to start with valid JSON-parseable bytes) it could produce garbage decoded data silently, which is worse than a clean failure.

Yes, a Kafka source can be configured today without `schema_registry` (`Config.SchemaRegistry *kafka.SchemaRegistryClient` is optional and `Validate()` only checks it when non-nil, see `drivers/kafka/internal/config.go:62-66`). That's a legitimate mode for JSON topics without wire-format framing — this issue is only about the case where wire-format framing IS detected but no registry is present to resolve it.

## Suggested fix

When `isConfluentWireFormat(data)` is true and `k.schemaRegistryClient == nil`, return a clear, actionable error…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama  treating Confluent-framed messages as JSON when schema_registry is not configured is by design. We cannot reliably determine whether a message is JSON or Avro just by looking at the message, since JSON does not have a fixed schema. We use sampling to infer the JSON schema, and this behavior was implemented accordingly. Could you let us know if this has caused any problems on your side?

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1189: arrow_writes: true breaks CDC deduplication on Iceberg/Glue destination — no equality-delete written, rows physically duplicate on every UPDATE
text:
Issue (completed): **Title:** `arrow_writes: true` breaks CDC deduplication on Iceberg/Glue destination — no equality-delete written, rows physically duplicate on every UPDATE

## Environment
- OLake UI: v0.5.0 (`olakego/ui`)
- OLake worker: v0.3.10 (`olakego/ui-worker`)
- Source connector: `olakego/source-mysql:v0.9.5`
- Source: MySQL 8.0 (Aurora MySQL 3.10), CDC via binlog (`ROW`, `FULL` row image, GTID on)
- Destination: Iceberg via Glue catalog, S3 storage
- Deployment: official `docker-compose.yaml` from the OLake repo, minimal profile (no Fusion/Amoro optimizer running)

## Summary
With the destination config `writer.arrow_writes: true`, any row that receives more than one CDC event in short succession (e.g. an application `INSERT` immediately followed by an `UPDATE`, a very common pattern — create a record, then fill in a few more fields moments later) gets written as **two separate physical rows** in the Iceberg table, with **no equality-delete file ever produced** to mark the older version as superseded. A plain `SELECT * FROM table` returns both versions forever. Setting `writer.arrow_writes: false` (Legacy writer) on an otherwise identical destination fixes this completely.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a MySQL source with `sync_mode: strict_cdc` (or `cdc`) on a table with `source_defined_primary_key: ["id"]`, `default_stream_properties.append_mode: false`.
2. Configure an Iceberg/Glue destination with `arrow_writes: true`.
3. Let the sync run against a table that receives real…

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1188: Iceberg legacy writer truncates timestamptz precision from microseconds to milliseconds
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- Olake version: v0.9.5 (commit `1005110bab4522a132a120ebd8064d147dda63f1`, also present on current `master` as of this report)
- Destination: Iceberg, REST catalog (AWS S3 Tables), normalized (typed-column) write mode, legacy gRPC/Java writer
- Source: Postgres, CDC (pgoutput)

## Description

Every `timestamptz` column written through the Iceberg legacy writer's normalized path loses sub-millisecond precision. Postgres stores `timestamptz` at microsecond resolution, and Iceberg's own `timestamptz` logical type is defined at microsecond resolution too, but the value that actually reaches Iceberg has been rounded down to the millisecond.

	if err != nil {

	}
	return &proto.IcebergPayload_IceRecord_FieldValue{
		Value: &proto.IcebergPayload_IceRecord_FieldValue_LongValue{LongValue: t.UnixMilli()},
	}, nil
```

- collaborator: Hi @erikcw , thanks for reporting this issue.
Please let us know if this is a blocker for your use case.

- contributor: Thanks for the quick response. Not a blocker for us today, we're still in a shadow/pilot phase and haven't found a consumer that depends on sub-millisecond precision. Filing it because Iceberg's `timestamptz` type is microsecond-precision by spec, so silently rounding down on write is a correctness issue even without a specific consumer hitting it yet. Not urgent on our end, but worth fixing whenever it's convenient.

- collaborator: **Where it happens**

Source drivers and `ReformatDate` keep full microseconds. The digits are lost only on the Go → Java gRPC hop of the legacy writer, and both sides assume milliseconds:

- Go sends epoch millis: `t.UnixMilli()` in [`destination/iceberg/legacy-writer/writer.go`](https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/blob/b16b34e4b259950b8ff7936e38ffe3f8cada4aaa/destination/iceberg/legacy-writer/writer.go#L296-L303)

Change both files together:

		}, nil
```

```

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1177: Iceberg destination: selected_columns excludes OLake metadata columns from CREATE-time schema, breaking _olake_id identifier field
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- Olake version: v0.9.5 (also present on current `master` as of this report)
- Destination: Iceberg, REST catalog (AWS S3 Tables)
- Source: Postgres, CDC (pgoutput)

## Description

When a stream's `selected_columns.columns` is a non-empty allowlist, the Iceberg destination excludes OLake's own metadata columns (`_olake_id`, `_olake_timestamp`, `_op_type`, `_cdc_timestamp`) from the schema sent to the writer at `GET_OR_CREATE_TABLE` time, because they are never listed in the user's column allowlist. The table therefore gets created (or evolved) without `_olake_id`, with no identifier field at all.

Once real records are written, `_olake_id` (and the other three metadata columns) get merged into the row data regardless of `selected_columns` (`destination/iceberg/iceberg.go`, `FlattenAndCleanData`: `maps.Copy(records[idx].Data, record.OlakeColumns)`), so `_olake_id` shows up as a "new column" against the table's actual schema. Schema evolution then adds it as a new field on an existing table, and Iceberg requires new fields on an existing table to be optional. Right after that, OLake calls `UpdateSchema.setIdentifierFields(["_olake_id"])`, which throws:

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Cannot add field _olake_id as an identifier field: not a required field
	at org.apache.iceberg.Schema.validateIdentifierField(Schema.java:168)
```

This repeats on every retry (with backoff) because `GET_OR_CREATE_TABLE` loads the already-created, already-broken table rath…

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1175: Postgres CDC: unchanged TOAST values are lost should we read them back from the source?
text:
Issue (completed): ## TL;DR

When an `UPDATE` doesn't touch a large out-of-line (TOASTed) column, Postgres leaves that column out
of the WAL. OLake currently writes a placeholder string for such columns into the destination. One fix is to read the value back from the source through a held `REPEATABLE READ` transaction. **It works and it is provably correct, but we have measured what it costs and would like input before committing to it.** A second approach reconstructing the value from the destination is tracked in the companion issue and puts zero load on the source (here postgres database).

---

## 1. The problem

A tuple must fit in an 8 KB page. Postgres moves large variable-length values (`text`, `jsonb`,
`bytea`, …) into a companion TOAST table, leaving an 18-byte pointer behind. When you update a row
**without changing that column**, Postgres does not rewrite it, so there is nothing to put in the
WAL. Logical replication sends a marker instead:

> `Byte1('u')` "Identifies unchanged TOASTed value (the actual value is not sent)."
> [PostgreSQL protocol docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/protocol-logicalrep-message-formats.html)

This is exact, not a heuristic. The protocol tells us precisely which columns are affected.

### What OLake does today

`pkg/waljs/pgoutput.go` writes the literal string `__olake_unavailable_value__` into the column.

Before Postgres moves a value out of the row, **it tries to compress it first**. Only if the value is
*still* too large after compression does…

Discussion:

- collaborator: Closing in favor of #1176.
- Re-reading from the source needs a transaction held open for the whole CDC run, which stops vacuum from cleaning up.
- Measured on a busy source: 10× database growth, ~14× CPU per unit of work.
- OLake should not put extra load on the user's database.
- Unchanged TOAST values will be read back from the destination instead.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1069: Postgres CDC cannot run against a read-replica: `pg_current_wal_lsn()` errors during recovery
text:
Issue (completed): ### What happens

Point the Postgres driver at a physical standby and every CDC run dies before any data moves:

```
failed to get slot position: ERROR: recovery is in progress (SQLSTATE 25006)
```

### Why

`pkg/waljs/replicator.go` builds the slot lookup with `pg_current_wal_lsn()`:

```go
ReplicationSlotTempl = "SELECT plugin, slot_type, confirmed_flush_lsn, pg_current_wal_lsn() as current_lsn FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE slot_name = '%s'"
```

That is a WAL control function, and it raises `recovery is in progress` on a standby. The standby equivalent is `pg_last_wal_replay_lsn()`. Nothing branches on `pg_is_in_recovery()`, so there is no path through this that works on a replica.

`GetSlotPosition` runs from `Postgres.PreCDC` (`drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go`) on every CDC run, and again in the LSN wait loop in `replicator.go`, so it fires immediately rather than partway through a sync.

### Why it matters

Postgres 16 added logical decoding on standbys, so the slot can live on a replica and keep decode load off a busy primary. The rest of the driver already looks compatible: `pg_replication_slot_advance()` is allowed on a standby for slots local to it, and `IdentifySystem` returns the replay position there. This one expression is the whole blocker.

The MSSQL driver picked up read-replica support in #949 and #991. This is the Postgres counterpart.

### Reproduction

PostgreSQL 18, a streaming replica built with `pg_basebackup -R`, `wal_level=logical` and `hot_standb…

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1014: Bug: Concurrent record filtering causes out-of-order data corruption
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description
Concurrent filtering in `utils/typeutils/filter.go` scrambles record order. 
**Impact:** Processing CDC events out-of-order leads to data corruption (e.g., applying an older `UPDATE` after a newer one, or `DELETE` before `INSERT`).
## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a pipeline with a filter.
2. Ingest a batch of ordered records.
3. Observe the output from `FilterRecords`—the records are shuffled due to non-deterministic goroutine execution and mutex locking.
## Expected behavior
Filtered records must strictly retain their original sequence.
## Actual behavior
Records are appended to the `filtered` slice randomly as goroutines complete.
## Proposed Solution
Instead of appending directly via a mutex, either:
1. Process records sequentially (safest/simplest).
2. Concurrently evaluate conditions into an index-mapped boolean array, then sequentially build the final filtered slice.

Discussion:

- none: Evaluating predicates concurrently into an index-addressed result array and compacting in a second ordered pass preserves sequence without giving up parallel predicate work. The implementation should also define how a predicate error or panic affects the batch: cancel remaining workers and return no partial reordered output, rather than silently dropping an index. A deterministic test can insert per-record delays in reverse order and verify that surviving CDC records retain their original sequence across many runs.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#984: Postgres CDC to S3 Parquet sets large jsonb / LOB column to null
text: Issue (completed): ## Summary When using Olake with PostgreSQL as the source and S3 Parquet as the destination, some `jsonb` columns are being written as `null` during CDC sync. This looks similar to the LOB/null column issue seen with AWS DMS. ## Environment - Source: PostgreSQL - Destination: S3 Parquet - Sync mode: CDC - Affected column type: `jsonb` - Example affected column: `invoice_details` ## Issue During CDC, the `jsonb` column becomes `null` in the destination Parquet files, even though the source PostgreSQL table contains non-null values. The affected `jsonb` values are relatively large. Most values in this column are around 3 KB to 15 KB. ## Expected behavior The `jsonb` column should be replicated correctly to S3 Parquet during CDC, preserving the original value from PostgreSQL. ## Actual behavior The `jsonb` column is written as `null` in the destination during CDC for affected rows. ## Impact This causes data loss in the destination because important JSON payloads are missing after CDC replication. Using append-only mode with query-side deduplication may work as a temporary workaround, but CDC mode should ideally preserve the full `jsonb` value. ## Questions 1. … Discussion: - collaborator: @Rtunc ,Thanks for reporting this issue and for the detailed investigation. Regarding your questions: 1. **Is there currently a size limit for jsonb / LOB columns in PostgreSQL CDC?** Large `jsonb` values can be affected during CDC because PostgreSQL WAL records may not contain the full value for TOASTed columns. In such cases, the column value may appear as `null` in the destination. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/storage-toast.html 2. **Could this be related to PostgreSQL TOASTed values?** Yes, this is related to PostgreSQL TOAST handling for large column values. 3. **Is there any configuration to force Olake to fetch full values for large jsonb columns during CDC?** At the moment, Olake does not support fetching full TOASTed jsonb values during CDC. As a workaround, you can use append-only mode with query-side deduplication. Alternatively, if you're okay with enabling REPLICA IDENTITY FULL on the affected table, we can help you with a quick fix. 4. **Is support for large jsonb / LOB columns in CDC planned?** Yes, support for large TOASTed `jsonb` / LOB columns in CDC is planned and is something we intend to address in a future release. - collaborator: We have resolved this issue and merged the fix, so closing this issue if you have any query left then feel free to reopen.

Currently when a source doesn't support CDC sync the default sync mode is set as incremental in streams.json . And the cursor field which is used to track new records is set to blank in that case, so that user can select the best suited field for it. Select the available cursor fields 0th value and set it as cursor field while generating the streams.json

4. Wait 2-3  mins
5. Check MySQL status ( queries are still running)

## Expected behavior

1. Kill queries that are already running in database ( MySQL/etc..)
2. Stop loading process and exit

Discussion:

- collaborator: @lkzcgfvf we have tried reproducing this issue internally, and not able to do it. Could you please share the worker logs for the affected job.

- none: yes, its still a problem. 
- What exactly UI does to stop job that is running? 
- If job is running with 10+ threads - how does it stop running query in every thread?

- collaborator: @lkzcgfvf 

> What exactly UI does to stop job that is running?

In OLake, A Job is a Temporal workflow (a process). When you click **Cancel Run**, the UI sends a cancellation request to the workflow. Once the workflow context is cancelled, the workflow begins shutting down gracefully and the job is cancelled.

> If job is running with 10+ threads - how does it stop running query in every thread?

Since all the threads belong to the same workflow, when the workflow context is cancelled all the connections to the database instance from that workflow are closed. 

---

Also, could you please let us know which one of this are you facing:

1. The database query remains in the `EXECUTING` state even after the job is cancelled.
2. The job state in the OLake UI does not change to `CANCELLED` after clicking **Cancel Run**.
3. Both of the above.

and share the logs of the Job of the affected Jobs. You can find an option to download the logs in the **Jobs Logs and History** page -> Affected Job's log

- none: option #3 ( Both of the above )
trying to rerpoduce to get logs

- collaborator: @lkzcgfvf  Regarding the issues:
 
**Issue #1:** This is a limitation of the MySQL driver. When a query is already executing, cancellation may not immediately terminate the query. The query will stop once the current scan operation completes. Since the table might not have a primary key, the scan can take longer to finish.
 
**Issue #2:** We'd like to investigate this further. Could you please share the logs for the affected job?

page_title: GitHub issue olake#938: Support for Case-Sensitive Column Names in Data Pipelines
text:
Issue (completed): ### Problem

Currently, Olake converts all column names to lowercase during data loads from source to destination (e.g., in Parquet files). This behavior can cause issues for systems where case sensitivity is enabled.

For example, in our setup using Amazon Redshift with case sensitivity enabled, this transformation leads to inconsistencies between the source and destination schemas.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce an option in the Olake UI to preserve the original case of column names during data transfer.

To maintain backward compatibility, this option can be disabled by default and made configurable for users who require case-sensitive column handling.

Discussion:

page_title: GitHub issue olake#937: declarative way to define sources, destinations and jobs
text:
Issue (completed): ### Problem

Right now we need to configure sources, destinations and jobs by hand

We can't easily replicate one olake setup to another olake setup

### Solution

Be able to define sources, destinations and jobs using yaml files

Discussion:

- none: @sibelius Thanks for raising this.

OLake already supports defining source, destination, and stream/catalog configuration as JSON files and running them through the CLI, 

for example:
`olake sync --config source.json --destination destination.json --catalog streams.json`

These files can already be versioned in Git, copied across environments, templated, and used from CI/CD, cron, Kubernetes Jobs, etc.

I want to better understand the gap you’re trying to solve with YAML specifically. Is the main ask about the file format itself, or about having a more declarative/GitOps-style workflow for defining sources, destinations, and jobs as reusable resources?

For example, JSON could also represent a declarative model for sources, destinations, and jobs. The larger missing piece may be an `apply`/reconcile workflow that can create or update OLake-managed resources from files, rather than YAML parsing alone.

Would love to understand what YAML enables in your workflow that the current JSON-based config does not, or whether the request is more about first-class GitOps/IaC support.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#926: improvement: wire SIGINT/SIGTERM into root context for graceful shutdown
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem

OLake does not wire OS signals (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) into its root `context.Context`. When the operating system delivers a clean-shutdown signal — Kubernetes pod eviction, Karpenter node consolidation, `docker stop`, or Ctrl-C in a dev shell — the process exits immediately, without giving the CDC / backfill / destination-writer paths any chance to reach their existing `ctx.Done()` branches.

### Evidence

Searching the tree for any signal handling:

```
$ git grep -nE 'signal\.Notify|os\.Interrupt|syscall\.SIG(INT|TERM|HUP)' -- ':!LICENCE'
(no matches)
```

Confirmed on current `master` (`v0.6.5`).

The root command is built from cobra's default background context:

- `protocol/root.go` declares `RootCmd = &cobra.Command{...}` with no `SetContext` / `ExecuteContext` anywhere, so `cmd.Context()` inside every subcommand is `context.Background()` that never cancels on signals.
- `connector.go:18` — `protocol.CreateRootCommand(true, driver).Execute()` — uses plain `Execute()` (not `ExecuteContext`).
- `protocol/root.go:85` — `connector = abstract.NewAbstractDriver(RootCmd.Context(), ...)` — so `AbstractDriver.GlobalCtxGroup` / `GlobalConnGroup` are also rooted on a background context.

Meanwhile, the CDC / read paths already branch on `ctx.Done()` and would unwind cleanly if the context were cancellable:

- `pkg/waljs/pgoutput.go:47-108` — the pgoutput receive loop has `case <-ctx.Done(): return nil` as its top-level exit, and `ReceiveMessage` is called with a `conte…

page_title: GitHub issue olake#877: Job failed to run "Clear Destination" and stuck in "InProgress" state
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- **Deploy method**: Kubernetes using latest Helm chart
- **Olake version**:  0.4.1-0.5.1

## Description
If you add new table to the list of streams then  Olake runs "Clear Destination" for destination folder to remove any files in folder that will be used to store Parquet files for this new table. Its correct and expected, however if this API call to destination fails - then job stuck in "InProgress" state forever.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create destination with type Amazon S3 and point it to Google GCS bucket ( its compatible with S3 API)
2. Create job that will use this destination
3. Add  any table to the list of streams
4. Run sync, it should finish correctly
5. Add new table to the list of streams
6. You will see that "Clear Destination" job started. It generated error ( its expected)  and it stuck forever ( not expected)

Here is error message generated by worker
```
failed to clear destination: 
failed to drop the streams: 
failed to clear S3 files: 
failed to clear S3 prefix <source>/<table>: 
batch delete failed for filt Path <source>/<table>: 
BatchedDeleteIncomplete: 
some objects have failed to be deleted. caused by: 
failed to perform batch operation on "<source>/<table>/XYZ.parquet" to "tpt_olake": NotImplemented: 
A header or query you provided requested a function that is not implemented. status code: 400, request id: , 
host id: failed to perform batch operation on "<source>/<table>/XYZ.parquet" to "tpt_olake": NotImplemented: 
A header or…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @lkzcgfvf Since **clear-destination** is a destructive operation, we cannot allow it to fail in a partially completed state. In the event of an error, it should continue retrying indefinitely until the issue is resolved, ensuring consistency and preventing any half-applied changes. (This is an intended design decision)

In your case, as the clear-destination error is expected, we have an `api` to recover in-progress (failing) clear-destination operation. It cancels the `clear` operation and resumes the `sync` operation.

```bash
COOKIE_JAR="/tmp/olake.cookies"; trap 'rm -f "$COOKIE_JAR"' EXIT
curl --location --request POST 'http://localhost:8000/login' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"username":"admin","password":"password"}' \
  --cookie-jar "$COOKIE_JAR"

curl -i --location --request POST 'http://localhost:8000/internal/project/123/jobs/<JOB_ID>/clear-destination/recover' \
  --cookie "$COOKIE_JAR"
```

> Note: Please update the hostname, port and the job_id as per your configuration. 

**If data is already present in the destination for the affected stream, It is recommended to drop the data manually before continuing with this process of recover**

- none: @vishalm0509 @vaibhav-datazip 
I agree that retry logic is very important for this operation, however  "continue retrying indefinitely" could be dangerous approach.
Job that stuck in "Running" state forever and it 
1. doesnt generate error
2. keeps running and do not allow to run itself next scheduled run

As result it will break pipeline and nobody will notice. In my particular case job was in this state ~18 hours, CDC pipeline was not collecting data from MySQL and we didnt know about it.

I would propose to adjust retry logic 
1. add logic that split errors in 2 categories: recoverable and  non-recoverable
2. add retry logic into recoverable errors ( network error, http 429, )
3. add configurable limits to retry logic ( ow many times to retry OR for how long)
4. stop work and exit with error for  non-recoverable error ( like AccessDenied OR  NotImplemented for DeleteObjects)

- collaborator: hey @lkzcgfvf , We will implement a fallback mechanism in few days, in case the S3 backend returns a NotImplemented error for DeleteObjects. Thanks for reporting this issue

MySQL allows to have empty string in ENUM columns even if empty string is not in the list of permitted  values.
From MySQL doc
 https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/enum.html
```
An enumeration value can also be the empty string ('') or NULL under certain circumstances:

If you insert an invalid value into an ENUM (that is, a string not present in the list of permitted values), the empty string is inserted instead as a special error value. This string can be distinguished from a “normal” empty string by the fact that this string has the numeric value 0. See [Index Values for Enumeration Literals](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/enum.html#enum-indexes) for details about the numeric indexes for the enumeration values.
If strict SQL mode is enabled, attempts to insert invalid ENUM values result in an error.

Issue (completed): ## Description

`AcknowledgeLSN` in `pkg/waljs/replicator.go` times out with a fatal `"LSN not updated after 5 minutes"` error when `ClientXLogPos` is behind the replication slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn`.

This happens in production when replicating databases with uneven WAL write/flush rates. We observed this on our OLake v0.5.0 deployment.

## Root Cause

There are two interacting issues:

**1. `ClientXLogPos` can regress behind `confirmed_flush_lsn`**

In `pgoutput.go:97` and `waljs.go:89`, the PrimaryKeepaliveMessage handler blindly assigns:

```go
p.socket.ClientXLogPos = pkm.ServerWALEnd
```

`ServerWALEnd` carries the WAL *flush* position, which can lag behind the WAL *write* position. Meanwhile, `PreCDC` advances the slot to `pg_current_wal_lsn()` (the write position). This creates a window where `ClientXLogPos` (flush) < `confirmed_flush_lsn` (advanced to write position).

**2. `AcknowledgeLSN` uses strict equality polling**

```go
if slot.LSN == walPosition {
    return nil
}
```

When `walPosition` (ClientXLogPos) is behind `confirmed_flush_lsn`, PostgreSQL silently ignores the StandbyStatusUpdate because `confirmed_flush_lsn` cannot move backwards. The equality check never matches, and the function times out after 5 minutes.

## Production Evidence

From our deployment logs:

```
state LSN:              E/D8EA31B8  (from pg_current_wal_lsn via PreCDC advance)
confirmed_flush_lsn:    E/D8EA31B8
IdentifySystem XLogPos: E/D8E19108  (flush position, 9MB behind)
keepali…

- contributor: Hi team, I went thru the existing 2PC implementation in the Iceberg destination : `olake_2pc_state` with `FullRefreshCommittedIDs` for idempotent chunk tracking across backfill retries. 
Would like to bring the same to the parquet writer. Can this be assigned to me?

- contributor: Hey @nayanj98 , wanted to share my design before diving into code, since it requires a few decisions I wanted to get the team's thoughts on:

 _Where 2PC actually matters for parquet :_
- Only during the backfill phase of CDC and incremental streams. Full-refresh streams call `DropStreams()` at the start of every sync invocation (I traced this in `sync.go`), which wipes the full stream path and resets state. Hence, no 2PC needed there.

### Core design

My approach would be to use a **per-thread committed manifests** strategy, so after a chunk's parquet files are written and uploaded successfully, we write a single file as the commit gate:
`_olake_2pc/<threadID>.committed` → content: JSON array of the exact parquet file paths that chunk wrote

#### _Setup() (first thread for the stream)_:
 List `_olake_2pc/*.committed` → extract threadIDs → return as `FullRefreshCommittedIDs` in `*MetadataState` (backfill.go's skip check picks this up automatically)
If uncommitted threadIDs found (i.e. crash recovery): traverse stream path, delete any `.parquet` file whose path isn't listed in any committed manifest

#### _Close()_:
Here we write `_olake_2pc/<threadID>.committed` with the file path…

- collaborator: @siiddhantt Will check with the backend team and get back to you.

- collaborator: @siiddhantt Thanks for sharing the design. Some clarification regarding where 2PC is needed: in OLake, 2PC is required across all sync modes, Initial Full Refresh, CDC, and Incremental, not just CDC/incremental backfill.
For CDC and Incremental syncs, the key requirement is that the state should be persisted at the same point as the destination commit (similar to the Iceberg implementation). This ensures that even if state file save fails afterward, the sync can safely resume from the last committed point in the destination without missing/duplicating the data, including for multi-stream jobs.
For Full Refresh as well, we still need commit tracking. The requirement there is to track which chunks have been successfully committed so resume after failure do not reprocess already committed chunks. 
To understand how this is handled in the Iceberg destination, you can also refer to this PR: https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/pull/698
Please let us know if you run into any issues or if there are any design decisions you'd like to discuss further.

- contributor: Thanks for the clarification, @nayanj98 . I’ve updated the implementation direction accordingly.

The Parquet 2PC workplan now covers all three paths:
- Full Refresh: tracks committed chunk/thread IDs so retries can skip already committed chunks.
- Incremental: persists the destination-side cursor metadata at the same point as the Parquet commit.
- CDC: persists the committed LSN in destination metadata and recovers from it if the external state file is stale or was not saved.

I followed the Iceberg pattern from #698 for the state recovery contract, but now adapting it for Parquet by storing table-local metadata under `<namespace>/<table>/_olake_2pc/`, since Parquet does not have an Iceberg catalog commit layer. 
Then I'm also adding orphan cleanup for prepared-but-uncommitted Parq

page_title: GitHub issue olake#853: Bug: PostCDC write ordering causes irrecoverable LSN mismatch between OLake state and PostgreSQL replication slot
text:
Issue (completed): ## Bug Description

There is a write-ordering issue in `PostCDC` and `PreCDC` that causes OLake's persisted cursor (LSN) to advance **ahead** of the PostgreSQL replication slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn`. Once this happens, the `validateGlobalState` check triggers a non-retryable error requiring a full "clear destination" — which is destructive and operationally painful for large datasets.

## Root Cause

In [`drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go:81-91`](https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/blob/main/drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go#L81-L91):

```go
func (p *Postgres) PostCDC(ctx context.Context, _ int) error {
    defer waljs.Cleanup(ctx, p.replicator.Socket())
    select {
    case <-ctx.Done():
        return ctx.Err()
    default:
        socket := p.replicator.Socket()
        p.state.SetGlobal(waljs.WALState{LSN: socket.ClientXLogPos.String()})  // ① writes to disk
        return waljs.AcknowledgeLSN(ctx, p.client, socket, false)              // ② tells PostgreSQL
    }
}
```

`SetGlobal()` calls `LogState()` which **synchronously writes the state file to disk** before `AcknowledgeLSN()` sends the `StandbyStatusUpdate` to PostgreSQL. If the process crashes, gets OOM-killed, or AcknowledgeLSN fails/times out between steps ① and ②:

- OLake's state file has LSN X (already flushed to disk)
- PostgreSQL's replication slot still has the old LSN Y (where Y < X)
- On restart, `validateGlobalState` detects the mismatch and returns a **non-retryable error**

The same pattern exists in …

Please add support for creating and managing OLake jobs from JSON (config-as-code), while keeping full parity in the UI for viewing, scheduling, and modifying those same jobs.

Today, job setup is primarily UI-driven. For teams operating many pipelines/environments, we need:

4. Export existing UI jobs back to JSON.
5. Round-trip compatibility:
   - JSON -> UI -> JSON should be stable and predictable.

- `Export JSON` on each job.

  - `GET /jobs/{id}/export` for canonical JSON

- Versioned schema (e.g., `schema_version`).
- Validation with clear field-level errors.
- Backward-compatible migrations when schema evolves.

- Schedule should be fully representable in JSON.
- UI schedule edits should update underlying JSON model.
- Timezone and cron handling …

page_title: GitHub issue olake#848: Feature request: Continue job on per-table failure (skip_failed_tables) instead of failing entire sync
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem
In multi-table sync jobs, a single table failure currently causes the entire job to fail.  
For CDC migrations, this blocks throughput when only a subset of tables are problematic.

## Requested behavior
Add a job-level option to continue processing remaining tables when one table fails.

Example config intent:
- `skip_failed_tables: true` (or similar)
- On failure of table `X`, OLake marks `X` as failed, logs error details, and proceeds with table `Y`.

## Why this matters
- Large table sets often include a few edge-case tables (datatype/PK/chunking issues).
- We can still make progress on healthy tables while isolating blockers.
- This reduces rerun cycles and operational overhead.

## Expected output/observability
When enabled:
1. Per-table status in final summary:
   - `succeeded_tables`
   - `failed_tables`
   - `skipped_tables` (if applicable)
2. Exit code semantics:
   - Optional: non-zero only if all tables fail, or configurable strict mode.
3. Error report artifact:
   - machine-readable list (CSV/JSON) of failed tables + reason.

## Suggested config shape
```yaml
continue_on_table_error: true
max_table_failures: 0   # 0 = unlimited, or stop after N failures

Backward compatibility
Default should preserve current behavior (false / fail-fast) unless explicitly enabled.
Real-world use case
We are running CDC across many MSSQL tables; some tables fail due to connector edge cases (e.g., GUID boundary handling), but many others sync successfully.

I'm using MySQL 8.0.14 and running OLake in CDC mode with S3/Parquet as destination. In MySQL I start transaction, insert row and then update this row several times in the same transaction. After that I commit transaction and run OLake to get changes that I made. As result I get Parquet file which has all operations that I made ( c, u, u)  but with the same value in "_cdc_timestamp" column. I understand that "_cdc_timestamp" column represents commit timestamp and that is why all rows have the same values. But it means that there is no column that could be used to sort these rows in the same way as they were made in MySQL. They are properly sorted in Parquet file but after these Parquet files are loaded into datawarehouse for further processing there is no way to sort rows properly to get the latest version of row because most of datawarehouses don't guarantee you sort order during reading data from table.  As result its not possible to achieve correct results in pipeline that process rows from Parquet files.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#750: Add Structured Error Classification & Retry Strategy for Source Connectors
text:
Issue (completed): **Problem Statement**

Currently, errors raised by different source connectors (Postgres, MySQL, Kafka, Parquet, etc.) are handled inconsistently.
All failures are treated similarly, even though some errors are retryable (network, timeout) while others are fatal (schema mismatch, permission issues).

**This makes:**

Debugging difficult

Retries inefficient

Logs less actionable

Proposed Solution

Introduce a standard error classification and retry strategy across all connectors.

**Key Requirements:**

Define common error categories:

Retryable (network, transient failures)

Non-retryable (auth failure, invalid config)

Centralize error handling logic

Apply retry policies only where applicable

Improve error messages with context (source, stage, reason)

Ensure backward compatibility with existing connectors

page_title: GitHub issue olake#707: MySQL ENUM datatype doesnt work correctly in CDC mode
GitHub issue olake#706: fix: float values from binlog are not always same as the output of select * query of db
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

In MySQL, there can be a difference between the actual value stored in a column and the value displayed when running a `SELECT * FROM table` query.

For example, consider a `FLOAT` (float32) column in MySQL. A value inserted as `12345.678912345678` may be displayed as `12345.679` when queried using the MySQL CLI. This is due to MySQL’s default display formatting and rounding behavior for floating-point types.

However, when syncing this data using OLake’s Iceberg Writer or Parquet Writer, the value is captured as the actual stored value (`12345.678912345678`) rather than the rounded value shown in the MySQL CLI (`12345.679`).

This behavior should be corrected so that the synced data matches the value displayed by MySQL during a `SELECT` query, ensuring consistency between source reads and downstream data consumers.

---

https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/blob/765752b2cae164eb5d73cef75365570ea8e22c4a/pkg/binlog/filter.go#L97-L101

---

###### This issue was generated by [todo-issue](https://github.com/DerJuulsn/todo-issue) based on a `TODO` comment in 765752b2cae164eb5d73cef75365570ea8e22c4a. It's been assigned to @badalprasadsingh because they committed the code.

Discussion:

- collaborator: hey @vimla01 , your understanding is mostly correct, but make sure you don't manually "interpret" the data. 

A good approach would be:

1. first, understand why the select * query from the source provides such an output
2. second, how OLake retrieves the value which was actually inserted, rather than the one displayed by the query
3. and then, you can move on with the implementation

Thanks for picking up the issue.

- contributor: Thanks for the clarification.. @badalprasadsingh 
From my understanding, MySQL FLOAT is stored as binary float32 ,while the value shown in SELECT is rounded for display. Binlog exposes a higher-precision float64 representation, which is why OLake currently retrieves extra precision.
I’ve implemented this by enforcing MySQL FLOAT (float32) semantics on binlog values, without any manual formatting or interpretation 
 I’ll raise the PR once I’m assigned/approved to proceed. @nayanj98 
Thanks.

I have column in MySQL with datatype DECIMAL(11,2) which OLake internally represents as "number_small".
This is float32 and according to spec float 32 could represents 6-7 Significant digits only.
Sources
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-precision_floating-point_format
 https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-language/type-float?view=msvc-170

This causes problem with passing large decimal values to Parquet file ( loosing precision).
This is critical to work financial data with precision 8 numbers and more.

## Steps to reproduce

In Mysql I have these values
157640.87
161864.63

OLake converts it to 
157640.875
161864.625

**Olake version**:   v0.3.5

## Proposed solution
Consider ALL decimal columns as "number" which is double(float64)  which supports 15-16 Significant digits

page_title: GitHub issue olake#675: MariaDB Source Support
text:
Issue (completed): ### Problem

When trying to create a CDC task with a MariaDB RDS instance the version returned from Maria does not correlate to the appropriate MySQL version and the check within pkg/jdbc/jdbc.go returns the wrong command to determine whether CDC can be enabled on the task.

`query := utils.Ternary(majorVersion > 8 || (majorVersion == 8 && minorVersion >= 4), jdbc.MySQLMasterStatusQueryNew(), jdbc.MySQLMasterStatusQuery()).(string)`

In our example we are trying to connect to MariaDB 10.11.13 which returns the func `MySQLMasterStatusQueryNew` and not the supported command in func `MySQLMasterStatusQuery`. 

The error surfaced associated with this is `Query 1 ERROR at Line 1: : You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near 'LOG STATUS' at line 1`.

### Solution

Due to the compatibility between MariaDB and MySQL especially in the CDC space I wouldn't recommend cloning the driver and changing the version logic, I think the overhead there would be more than it's worth. 

The suggestion I had was to evaluate the Engine string within the pkg/jdbc/jdbc.go `MySQLVersion` function and resolve to the associated MariaDB version to MySQL for example in our instance:

MariaDB: `SELECT @@version` = 10.11.13-MariaDB-log

Within the `MySQLVersion` check for the string instance of `MariaDB` and if so present resolve to a MySQL version string. Ideally `10.11.13-MariaDB-log` would resolve to the `MySQLMas…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @jaytringfm We are picking this issue up internally and we will be releasing the fix in the coming versions. Thank you very much for getting this out here!

- collaborator: Hi @jaytringfm , 

A PR #677 has been raised to address this issue. The fix includes:

1. **MariaDB detection**: The code now properly detects MariaDB vs MySQL by checking the version string
2. **Query selection**: MariaDB will always use `SHOW MASTER STATUS` (the correct syntax) instead of `SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS`

This will be fixed in the next version of OLake once the PR is merged and released. You can upgrade to the new version to use MariaDB as a CDC source.

Thanks for reporting this issue!
